what_it_does: Identifies the root filesystem during boot preparation.
reason: The identifier participates in boot preparation and root filesystem selection; it is not merely document content.

what_it_does: Supplies platform-specific kernel arguments and boot console commands.
reason: Removing the platform specifications loses platform-specific boot configuration capability; effects extend beyond the installer.

what_it_does: Selects the boot loader entry directory through a symbolic link.
reason: Removing the link makes the selected boot entries unavailable through the boot loader path.

what_it_does: Provides boot entries selecting operating system deployments.
reason: Boot entries determine which operating systems and kernels can be started; removing them removes those boot choices.

what_it_does: Reports the result of initial provisioning.
reason: The report records past execution of provisioning; records of the past are exempt.

what_it_does: Records completed password-file permission repair, suppressing repeat execution.
reason: The completion stamp records past repair; S2.2-6 exempts records of the past without excluding records consulted later.

what_it_does: Records the last completed update of system configuration.
reason: The timestamp records a completed update. The records-of-the-past exemption does not exclude timestamps used for subsequent scheduling.

what_it_does: Selects executable implementations, loadable libraries, and manual pages.
reason: MUST: executable and library links; NOT: four *-man links, which only select documentation. Full member mapping is in notes.

what_it_does: Configures shared container-image signature lookup locations.
reason: Shared signature configuration governs verification by multiple image tools, so the single-program setting exemption does not apply.

what_it_does: Retains a backup of previous group definitions.
reason: This backup records previous group definitions rather than defining current accounts or access rights.

what_it_does: Retains a backup of previous group authentication records.
reason: The backup is a record of the past, explicitly exempt even though the active database concerns access.

what_it_does: Displays informational login messages about network addresses and server key fingerprints.
reason: Both snippets are informational text; removing them removes displayed content, not login functionality.

what_it_does: Selects devices available for logical volume management.
reason: The device selection controls available storage operations across LVM tools, not a setting confined to one program.

what_it_does: Controls automatic loading of the nouveau kernel driver.
reason: The blacklist changes which kernel code can load, affecting the operating system beyond the configuration reader.

what_it_does: Retains a backup of previous account definitions.
reason: A backup of the account database is a past record, not the current account definitions explicitly required by S2.2-15.

what_it_does: Provides applications with resolver configuration through the system resolver link.
reason: Removing this shared resolver link disrupts name-resolution configuration for applications; its effect is not confined to one program.

what_it_does: Configures shared password-quality checking through libpwquality.
reason: The policy changes which passwords multiple utilities accept; it is neither a password value nor a single-program setting.

what_it_does: Retains a backup of previous password and account-aging records.
reason: The backup stores previous account state; the records-of-the-past exemption applies.

what_it_does: Retains a backup of previous subordinate group identifier allocations.
reason: The backup records past allocations rather than providing the active allocation rules.

what_it_does: Retains a backup of previous subordinate user identifier allocations.
reason: The backup records past allocations rather than providing the active allocation rules.

what_it_does: Defines permission to execute commands with elevated privileges.
reason: Both sudo policy files govern the right to become superuser, which is explicitly required.

what_it_does: Provides explanatory documentation about system configuration files.
reason: The README is document content; removing it removes only that explanation.

what_it_does: Enables, aliases, masks, and connects system and user services.
reason: The presets and links control program activation and independent services; their effects extend beyond systemd itself.

what_it_does: Records the last completed update of variable system data.
reason: The timestamp records a completed update. The records-of-the-past exemption does not exclude timestamps used for subsequent scheduling.

what_it_does: Caches downloaded repository metadata and dependency-solving indexes.
reason: All listed files are cached repository material or indexes; removing them requires fetching or recomputation rather than removing installed functionality.

what_it_does: Executes shell commands when a login shell exits.
reason: Bash executes this file with shell rights; executable settings count as code.

what_it_does: Executes shell initialization commands at login.
reason: Shell startup files are explicitly required, even when commands set environment values.

what_it_does: Executes initialization commands for interactive shells.
reason: Shell startup files are explicitly required; settings expressed as executed commands remain code.

what_it_does: Stores public keys authorized to log in to the account.
reason: The sole content-bearing member is an authorized login-key file; account login keys are explicitly required.

what_it_does: Stores a work-note document.
reason: The recorded creation command writes ordinary prose; removing the note removes only its content.

what_it_does: Executes shell commands when a login shell exits.
reason: The shell executes logout commands with its own rights; they are code, including when used as settings.

what_it_does: Executes shell initialization commands at login.
reason: Shell startup files are explicitly required by S2.2-10.

what_it_does: Executes initialization commands for interactive shells.
reason: Shell startup files are explicitly required; executable settings are code.

what_it_does: Records completion of initial logical-volume device-list population.
reason: The completion stamp records a past action; S2.2-6 does not exclude historical records consulted by later service conditions.

what_it_does: Records users' most recent login events.
reason: The last-login database records the past, explicitly exempt under S2.2-6.

what_it_does: Stores deployment history records.
reason: The sole content-bearing member is a deployment history record; history is explicitly exempt.

what_it_does: Links to explanatory documentation about system logs.
reason: The link provides document content; removing it only loses access to that explanation through this path.

what_it_does: Stores historical audit events.
reason: The audit log is an explicitly exempt record of the past.

what_it_does: Stores historical system and user journal events.
reason: Both journal files are logs; records of the past are explicitly exempt.

what_it_does: Provides an alternate path to the boot directory.
reason: The link target is known, but inventory and consulted documentation do not identify consumers relying on this alias.

what_it_does: Tracks installed bootloader components and pending updates.
reason: Current installed-component and pending-update state governs bootloader update operations; it is not merely a historical log.

what_it_does: Supplies bootloader code, boot commands, module indexes, and translated messages.
reason: MUST: boot code, commands, fs.lst; NOT: locale/*.mo; UNKNOWN: other index roles not established. Exact member partitions and supporting sources are in notes.

what_it_does: Supplies the boot kernel, initial filesystem image, and kernel integrity digest.
reason: Kernel and initial filesystem enable boot; the associated digest supports kernel integrity checking. These implement boot functionality rather than user content.

what_it_does: Provides synchronization for concurrent account-database modification.
reason: Inventory does not show whether the lock is held; removing a live lock and removing an unused recreatable file have different effects.

what_it_does: Maintains selections and link groups for alternative command and library implementations.
reason: Administrative selections govern installation and maintenance of executable and library links used across programs.

what_it_does: Supplies a PAM configuration for switchable authentication.
reason: Neither file contents nor enabled authentication mechanisms are captured; documentation identifies possible roles but cannot establish this file's actual effects.

what_it_does: Links authentication-related desktop settings and locks into dconf configuration.
reason: Actual settings and locks are absent from the inventory; their effect may concern login availability or only the login-screen interface.

what_it_does: Exposes switchable-auth configuration to the PAM service loader.
reason: The target's contents and authentication effects are not supplied; its filename alone cannot determine whether it changes login rules or presentation.

what_it_does: Stores security policy inputs, compiled policy, transaction metadata, and locks.
reason: MUST: policy and labeling inputs; NOT: commit_num transaction record; UNKNOWN: lock state and derived-file reconstruction. Exact member partitions are in notes.

what_it_does: Provides SSH server identity keys, public-key copies, and password-login policy.
reason: MUST: three private keys and password-login policy; NOT: three .pub files supplied as copyable public content. Member names are in notes.

what_it_does: Records completion of variable-directory security labeling.
reason: The stamp records completed labeling; the past-record exemption does not exclude records subsequently consulted to avoid repetition.

what_it_does: Stores network state, identity seed, DHCP lease information, and connection history.
reason: MUST: NetworkManager.state, secret_key, *.lease; NOT: seen-bssids, timestamps; UNKNOWN: NetworkManager-intern.conf without values. Sources and member rationale are in notes.

what_it_does: Stores a checksum associated with authentication configuration management.
reason: The checksum's exact consumer and deletion consequences could not be established from inventory or consulted public documentation.

what_it_does: Exposes kernel-to-userspace RPC authentication communication endpoints.
reason: The pipe and associated information expose RPC authentication requests between kernel and daemon; they provide functionality rather than stored document content.

what_it_does: Makes the package database available through its conventional location.
reason: Removing the database path prevents package-management operations using that location; the link supplies operational access, not merely readable content.

what_it_does: Enables persistent user services and stores timer history with service-state directories.
reason: MUST: linger marker; NOT: timers/stamp-*; UNKNOWN: three other empty service-state directories. The timers directory contains exempt history; member partition is in notes.

what_it_does: Stores shell initialization code and build-description content with an empty key directory.
reason: MUST: .bash_logout, .bash_profile, .bashrc; NOT: buildinfo and its empty JSON documents; UNKNOWN: empty .ssh directory's operational requirement.

what_it_does: Provides remaining directory entries without separately inventoried content-bearing members.
reason: Inventory names the directories but does not establish all consumers, recreation behavior, or which operations require these existing directory entries.
